## Question 2 (15-points)

For question 2, we are going to use the `mtcars` data set in base R.

a) Pull up the help file and copy the description of the data set into your document. 

b) Use code to define the data type that the `vs` variable is in the `mtcars` data set. Based on the description in the help file, do you think R should read this variable differently? Why or why not?

c) Index the `mtcars` data frame to pull out the `mpg` value of the Datsun 710 car. Name this R object `Datsun`

[Hint:https://dereksonderegger.github.io/570L/5-matrices-data-frames-and-lists.html#data-frames-1](https://dereksonderegger.github.io/570L/5-matrices-data-frames-and-lists.html#data-frames-1)


d) In this question we are going to learn how to write in-line R code! Read section 10.2 of the following book [here](https://zsmith27.github.io/rmarkdown_crash-course/lesson-5-code-chunks-and-inline-code.html#inline-code)

In short: Code results can be inserted directly into the text of a .qmd file by enclosing the code with `r `.

Write the following setence: "The mean mpg for the Datsun 710 car in 194 was" and use in-line code with the R object you created in c to report the mean mpg for the Datsun 710 car. Note, this is not a formal code chunk! This is a quick way to report result in-line with your text!

Create a new variable called mpg_category in a data set called `mtcars2`, based on whether mpg is above or below 20. ## Question 4 (10-points)

For this question, I'm asking you to compare and contrast the two for loops. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
for (i in 1:nrow(mtcars)) { if (mtcars$mpg[i]>25) { print(mtcars$mpg[i]) } else { print("MPG is 25 or less") } }

# vs

for (i in 1:nrow(mtcars)) {
  if (mtcars$mpg[i] > 25) {
    print(mtcars$mpg[i])
  } else {
    print("MPG is 25 or less")
  }
}
```
:::



a) Do both run with no errors and give you output? Yes or no? 

b) Why is the second for loop easier to read? Come up with at least three rules learned by comparing both sets of code, and list them below. Put two dashes `--` before your comment to make a list. Ex. 

`-- I see that...`
